checks: Checked e0478eebc433b0f6:04 §§3–4 (9)–(15) and :05 §5 (16). The source uses raw mixed and ordinary area depth on the complete trace, with arbitrary nonnegative lambda.

Affine positive r and convexity of T give exact homothetic interpolation between the extremal fibers. Integer bases are exactly 0 through 5. The six squared radii sum to 591/16, and 16<591/32 verifies strict nonheaviness.

Every containing ambient halfspace pays at least own depth. A finite exposing tilt isolates base zero. At base one, for a given proper own cap, a sufficiently large negative slope in z−1 keeps all of base zero and strictly excludes every base ≥2. This yields D(1,x)≤f_T(x)+1/16.

Own depths scale by r², and their roots by r. The ordinary simplex maximum is 4/9 at the centroid. This verifies the three stated intercept and slope bounds. The mean of the base-zero and base-two slope terms is 2 lambda/3, and their intercept average minus 73/144 is exactly 3/16. Every base affine cost cancels in the same average.

For full-point costs (1,x) is the exact midpoint of (0,x/4) and (2,7x/4), and both F and affine costs have exactly the midpoint value. The averaged endpoint D lower bound minus the base-one upper bound is (9 f_T(x)−1)/16. Continuity and the strict centroid value 4/9 give the open region and the 3/16 centroid certificate.

dependencies.hypotheses: All actual finite compact fibers fit the anchored-cap continuity statement, so D is continuous on each and the mixed-plus-own maxima over each compact fiber are attained.
The proof supplies continuity of pointwise ordinary depth and exact sharp centroid depth for an ordinary full-dimensional planar simplex. Since T has area one, its normalized 4/9 is also raw.

overlap.comparison: It characterizes a scalar family of active optimizers. It does not cover arbitrary added affine costs or prove that the positive fiber in this exact six-site chain is uniformly hidden.
Its exposed-fiber equality yields the base-zero isolation after matching raw measures. Base one is not exposed and the two-slope finite tilt and midpoint exclusion used here are new conclusions.

summary: The six actual simplex fibers give a uniformly hidden base and an open region hidden from every full affine cost.
